title: Login page renders raw JSON debug state ("{"isAuthenticated":false}" / "{"currentUser":null}") above the welcome heading
description: When an unauthenticated visitor lands on the EcoExpense login page, two lines of raw JSON — `{"isAuthenticated":false}` and `{"currentUser":null}` — are rendered as plain visible text directly above the "Welcome to EcoExpense" heading. This is leftover debug output leaking internal authentication/session state into user-facing copy. It looks broken and unpolished to every visitor, and it exposes internal state field names to end users. It appears on every visit to the page for signed-out users (the paragraphs are rendered unconditionally in the signed-out branch of the LoginPage component).
expected_behavior: The login page should show only user-facing content: the "Welcome to EcoExpense" heading with the Sign in / Sign up buttons. Internal authentication state (isAuthenticated, currentUser) should never be rendered as visible text; any debug output belongs in the console or behind a dev-only flag, not in the page DOM.
actual_behavior:
Two `

` elements render `JSON.stringify(...)` of the auth hook's state on the page itself: the visitor sees `{"isAuthenticated":false}` and `{"currentUser":null}` as visible text above the welcome heading, on every load of the login page while signed out.

chain.text: In LoginPage.tsx, the LoginPage component pulls `isAuthenticated` and `currentUser` from useAuth() (line 11); when the user is signed out, the component renders its signed-out branch (lines 35-60).

This is not a purely aesthetic preference, not a low-contrast or display-correctness issue (the text renders exactly as authored — the problem is that debug content is authored into user-facing DOM at all), and not a functional failure — the sign-in flow itself is not broken. The report gives a concrete root cause (unconditional debug paragraphs in the signed-out branch of LoginPage.tsx), an actionable expected behavior and fix (remove the debug paragraphs; console logging already exists), and a clear visible impact on all signed-out users.
